ACT I

SCENE I. A road outside the town.

TRAVELLER.
You have the letter, and you do not read it.
What do you fear that paper will announce?
The hour is late, the candle nearly finished,
And still you stand there like a man of stone.

MERCHANT.
I have the letter and I know the writing.
The thing I fear is written plainly in it,
And having read it once I need not read again.
You are too quick to advise on what you do not know.

TRAVELLER.
Then hand it over, let me take the burden,
Because you have been carrying it a month.
A trouble that is shared becomes the lighter,
And what you carry by yourself will break you.

MERCHANT.
You cannot take it. It belongs to me.
The name upon the seal is mine, and yours
Does not appear at all. Now go to sleep.
I will be well enough by morning light.

TRAVELLER.
You will not. I have watched you three nights running,
And every single night you say the same,
And every single morning you are worse.
What is the thing that you are hiding from me?

MERCHANT.
A debt. A promise that was never kept.
A word I gave you when I was young and foolish,
Which now comes back to ask for what I lack.
There, you have it. Are you any happier?

TRAVELLER.
I am not happy. I am less afraid,
Which is a kind of happiness of sorts.
A debt can still be paid, a word withdrawn.
Come, we will find the money between us.
